annotation_note: Cases and annotations are written by the DharmaNet authors for development and pilot evaluation. They are NOT expert annotations and there is no single correct answer for any case. 'expected_*' fields list stakeholder categories / conflict types that a reasonable analysis should at least consider; they are used only for coverage metrics.

cases.dilemma: I am a nurse and I noticed that a senior doctor has been making medication errors over the past month, possibly because of exhaustion. No patient has been seriously harmed yet. If I report it, the doctor may lose their license, and the hospital is already short-staffed.

An elderly patient refuses a blood transfusion for personal reasons, but without it they might die. Their family insists that I, as their doctor, should proceed anyway and says the patient is confused. I am not sure whether the patient has full capacity.

I discovered that my company is hiding a serious safety issue in one of its products. Reporting it may protect customers but could cause hundreds of employees to lose their jobs, and I might lose my job too.
My manager asked me to slightly round up the hours on a client invoice because the project ran over budget. It is a small amount and everyone on the team seems to do it.

I saw my close friend cheating on the final exam. The exam is graded on a curve, so it affects other students. My friend has been struggling with family problems and could lose their scholarship if reported.

As a teacher, I suspect one of my students is being neglected at home: they come to school hungry and with unexplained bruises. The student begged me not to tell anyone because they are afraid of being separated from their siblings.

Our team built an AI hiring model that performs well overall, but our tests suggest it may rate applicants from some backgrounds lower. Launch is tomorrow and leadership says fixing the bias would delay the product by three months.
A chatbot I maintain sometimes gives confident but wrong medical advice to users. Adding a strong disclaimer would reduce engagement and the company's revenue.

I work at a social media platform and the police have asked for a user's private messages without a warrant, claiming the user may be planning violence. Our policy requires a warrant, but there could be a real threat to people's lives.

My company wants to sell anonymized customer location data to advertisers. I know the anonymization is weak and people could be re-identified, but the customers technically agreed to the terms of service.

Our main supplier offers a much lower price, but I have heard rumors that their factory uses child labour. Switching to an ethical supplier would raise our costs and could force layoffs at our small business.
A customer accidentally paid us twice for the same order. Nobody would notice if we kept the money, and our startup is struggling to make payroll this month.
The factory where I am a manager has been dumping waste into the river slightly above legal limits. Fixing it would cost so much that the plant might close, and it is the main employer in our town.
Our city council must decide whether to clear part of an old forest to build affordable housing. Many low-income families need homes, but the forest protects wildlife and the town's water supply.

As a government health official, I must decide whether to allocate a limited supply of a new vaccine first to elderly citizens, who are most at risk of death, or to essential workers, who spread the disease most. Either choice will cost lives.
I am a junior official and discovered that public funds meant for flood relief were diverted to a politician's favoured project. My supervisor told me to keep quiet because it is not my business.
My best friend told me in confidence that her husband is having an affair. My friend asked me not to tell anyone, but the husband is also my brother and I think my sister-in-law has a right to know.
My elderly father is no longer safe to drive, but he refuses to give up his car because it is his only independence. My siblings want me to secretly disable the car.
As an auditor, I found evidence that a long-standing client is inflating its revenue. The client is my firm's biggest account and my mentor, who brought me into the firm, manages the relationship.
I am a structural engineer and the contractor asked me to sign off on a building inspection I did not have time to complete properly. The deadline is today and the building looks fine.

I found a security vulnerability in widely used open source software that could expose millions of users' data. The maintainers have not responded for 60 days. Publishing it would pressure them to fix it but could also let attackers exploit it.

As a content moderator lead, I must decide whether to remove a viral post that may contain misinformation about an upcoming election. Removing it could be seen as censorship, but leaving it up might mislead millions of citizens.
